title: Retainer vs Hourly: session micro-model
content:
Quick brain-dump comparing two packaging levers for conversational products: retainer (monthly seat/slots with burst) vs hourly/session-based billing (time or compute units). Focus: unit economics at small-mid enterprise and SMB scale; how to hedge cold-cache / prompt-heavy workflows.

Context / assumptions (back of envelope):
- Model baseline: LlamaX-13B quantized serving variant. Token cost to Redwood (amortized infra + GPU ops per token): ~$0.0000025 / token (2.5e-6) at steady state with batching and caching assumptions.
- Average session length options: short chat = 200 tokens request + 300 tokens response -> 500 tokens; medium = 1k tokens; long = 5k tokens.
- Concurrent slot amortization: one guaranteed slot (warm KV) acts as 1 small reserved GPU thread equivalent. If customer purchases N slots, we assume 60% utilization on average.
- Customer SLO: p95 latency < 350ms; this implies we need margin on dedicated capacity. Extra 25% headroom cost.

Simple per-session cost math: (tokens * cost_per_token) * (1 + headroom) + fixed amortized slot cost.
- token_cost = 2.5e-6
- headroom multiplier = 1.25
- slot_monthly_cost_amortized_per_session = depends on sessions/day and slots; see examples.

Examples (rough):
1) SMB plan: pay-as-you-go session billing (no slot reserved)
- medium session (1k tokens): compute = 1000 * 2.5e-6 = $0.0025; with headroom ~ $0.0031 per session.
- add infra+overhead & billing take: target gross margin -> list price per session = $0.01 (small markup allowed for low friction).

2) Retainer slot model: monthly retainer buys 5 concurrent slots + monthly credit pool
- slot monthly cost (our internal): assume $120 per slot/month (includes reserved GPU share + infra). 5 slots -> $600/mo.
- expected throughput: if each slot supports ~300 sessions/day (short+medium mix) -> 1500 sessions/day -> ~45k sessions/month. Effective slot amortization per session = 600 / 45k = $0.0133.
- plus token cost per session (1k tokens) = $0.0031 -> total cost ~$0.0164. Price the retainer: $0.05 per session effective, or base retainer $600 + overage credits at $0.02/session.

Observations: retainer beneficial when high session volume and need for consistent latency. For low volume, retainer per-session price can look expensive vs payg.

Pricing levers / experiments to try (ideas):
- Hybrid: small monthly slot + incremental per-session credits. e.g., $200/mo for 2 slots + 10k credits -> good for growing SMBs.
- Session caps vs token caps: customers understand "60 sessions/day" easier than tokens; but tokens map better to cost. Consider converting tokens -> sessions for UX.
- Time-bucketed credits: larger credits for off-peak to encourage smoothing.
- SLA premium: +20% on retainer for 99.9% uptime / reserved burst.

Edge cases and risk items: 
- Cold-cache heavy workloads (long context recalc) blow up token cost. Mitigation: measure per-customer cold-cache ratio; offer "warm context" as addon or price by KV cache weight.
- Very long responses (>=10k tokens) should be gated and priced per-token explicitly.
- Abuse / spam: need per-seat rate caps and fraud detection; otherwise retainer economics break.

Product-level quick tier sketches (names are placeholders):
- Spark (payg micro): no slots, per-session billing; ideal for prototypes and low throughput.
- Beacon (starter retainer): 2 slots + small credit pool; predictable latency for small teams.
- Current (production retainer): 5 slots + SLA option + discounted per-session overage.
- Ramp (enterprise committed): custom slots, discounted bulk token price, dedicated region.

Back-of-envelope reconciliations to validate: 
- If average session token count goes up by 2x, payg per-session cost goes to ~$0.006 / session -> retainer advantage grows. Keep sensitivity table.
- If slot utilization falls below 30%, retainer is losing money; need utilization dashboards + auto-triggers for scale-down or suggest credits conversion.

Open questions / TODOs: 
- Calculate true per-token cost for other models (redwood-7B, redwood-34B) and various quantization levels; update token_cost constant.
- Create a simulation spreadsheet: inputs = slots, utilization, avg tokens/session, sessions/day, monthly retainer -> outputs: unit cost, margin at different price points. Linked linear: PR-378 for simulation work.
- UX: how to present sessions vs tokens in billing UI? run quick user interviews.
- Partner with SRE to get realistic slot monthly cost (current $120 is placeholder).

Notes to self: keep experiments small and track cohort margins by model family and by workload (Q&A vs longform). Demo idea: onboarding wizard that suggests pack (Spark/Beacon/Current/Ramp) based on a 7-day traffic export.

Random heuristics I like: price per-session in payg should be at least 3x computed cost to leave room for margins and support; retainer per-session effective price can be 5-8x cost but offset by predictability value.

End of scratchpad.
